Build Cycles · 4 a year

Thirteen weeks from now, you’ll have built something real.

You’ll pick a problem that matters to you, team up, and see it through — with mentors and a whole community behind you.

Register for this cycle
What you walk away with

Something real you helped build, proof of it on your profile, and people who’ve seen what you can do.

How you get there

Month one: dig into a real problem with your pod. Month two: decide what to build at the Hackathon. Month three: build it, test it, and show it.

What it takes

Six in-person events, a five-minute check-in each week, and the rest on your own time with your team.

Open source, on purpose

Everything a team builds here is an open-source community project. When the cycle’s over, you’re free to do whatever you want with it — and so is everyone else.

How it works

Three phases, one arc.

Problem Sprint · Weeks 1–5

The cycle starts by looking, not building. Everyone collects things they’ve actually seen, we map them together in the Triangulator, and pods form around the problems that keep showing up. By week 5, your pod picks one to own.

Frame Sprint · Weeks 6–9

Your pod digs into its problem — interviews, field visits, homework nobody assigned. At the Hackathon, all that digging becomes proposals: new ways of seeing the problem, and what to build about it. Then everyone votes.

Building · Weeks 10–13

Winning proposals become teams of 3–5. You build something real, test it with real people, and bring everything — the wins and the misses — back to the commons at the Showcase Summit.
